The teacher as reflective practitioner: design, implementation and evaluation
Caution: this information is subject to change

Intended learning outcomes:

Students have knowledge and understanding of: 

  • the concepts and terminology of educational research

  • research methods and research techniques within educational research.
     

Students can apply the scientific methods and techniques as used in researching relevant problems in education and are able to communicate research results (skills):

  • find relevant literature on educational research, read it critically, process and discuss it

  • collect, analyze, compare and contrast data from the educational field at an initial academic level

  • formulate research questions and answer these questions under supervision by mounting, methodically and creatively carrying out, and critically reviewing research fitting the research questions

  • reason and argue in a structured and scientific manner

  • express their own judgments and views clearly and succinctly in a relevant way both orally and in writing at an academic level. 
     

Students have the ability to (character):

  • judge and evaluate on formal grounds and in terms of content their own research and other products and those of fellow students

  • employ reasoning and arguing in the process of learning, to put forward relevant points of view and to understand and appreciate points of views of others, to share knowledge and contribute to discussions in a group 

  • reflect on their own qualities and skills, to draw conclusions with regard to their own development, and to take action to optimize their own learning trajectory 

  • orient themselves independently towards the educational sector or possible further studies.

Content:
The course provides a theoretical and methodological background for research in an educational context, in which lesson design, intervention and end products are being evaluated. We focus on the teacher who is doing research in educational practice. Nowadays in education, teachers are more and more expected to show an academic attitude. They should assume the role of reflective practitioners, who evaluate their educational practice and make innovations on the basis of research.
In educational evaluation research, three kinds of research can be distinguished: evaluation of the design, evaluation of the implementation (process evaluation) and evaluation of the obtained results or goals (product evaluation). In this course, these types of evaluation research will be dealt with in a theoretical manner and illustrated by using examples. Besides, students will be critically reviewing different cases, working with a research instrument (observation) and writing a proposal containing an educational intervention and the accompanying evaluative research.
The course consists of four parts. In the first part, we will deal with backgrounds on importance of research in education and the role of teachers as reflective practitioners. In the next parts, the three types of educational research (design, process and product evaluation), will be the focus of attention. There are three meetings on each research type: a lecture on the theoretical backgrounds, a lecture in which one or more examples are being discussed and a seminar in which we work on the assignment related to the kind of research.
 
Specifics:
The grade of the course is based on:
  • Written exam: 50%
  • Portfolio with three assignments: 50%
Students are required to attend all three seminars in which they work on the assignments for their portfolio.
Labour market orientation: this course is focused on the educational field and makes use of concrete, practical examples taken from this field. For prospective teachers in primary and secondary education this course provides a preparation for their role as reflective practitioner in their future workplace.
 
Required prerequisites:
Research Methodology, such as: Doing Research: methodology
 
Recommended prerequisites:
Some knowledge of educational practices
